newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-FALDO DENIES PLAYERS TRYING TO UNDERMINE TOUR IMAGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO DENIES PLAYERS TRYING TO UNDERMINE TOUR IMAGE.

text.p: Nick Faldo on Saturday denied a charge by former Ryder Cup captain Bernard Gallacher that he and new captain Seve Ballesteros had been trying to undermine the European Tour's image at a players' meeting earlier this week.
Gallacher was quoted in a British national newspaper as saying that there was "a danger that this wrangling will undermine the game's image with current sponsors and put off potential sponsors."
The meeting of some 50 players on Tuesday night was called and chaired by Ballesteros to discuss the quality of the golf courses being used on the Tour.

He convened the meeting in the wake of the poor greens at the Collingtree Park course in England during the British Masters two weeks ago and the easy state of the Nippenburg course in Stuttgart at the German Open the previous week.
Gallacher conceded there had been problems at the two venues and they would be put right.
Faldo, referring to the meeting, said: "I thought we were allowed freedom of speech, especially at a private meeting.
"There is nothing devious about sitting in a room discussing the condition of the golf courses. In fact I would have thought it was constructive," he said.
"All we want to know is that the team reviewing the courses before we play them is the best."
Faldo said when he first complained about the state of the courses and pinpointed it two years ago as one reason for his move to the U.S. Tour, he had been "shot down in flames."
He said that at Collingtree Park "the guys saw red. It was the last straw.""

Faldo added: "I think they (the Tour) will listen. From the rumblings they are getting about the meeting, they will see that the guys are pushing their message about what they want." He quipped: "We don't want heads to roll, we want the greens to roll."
